To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

hidden neurons behave as binary classifiers during training; the fuzzy, binary partitions that emerge during training embed the core information used for classification; these partitions are constant across training; and they are used during testing.
(1) during training, a neuron separates two input categories that are constant across training; (2) during testing, the fuzzy, binary separation encoded by a neuron is used to make predictions.

1) hidden neurons in a deep neural network trained through stochastic gradient descend behave like binary classifiers, 2) these classifiers are stable during training and are the core building blocks of the network, and 3) the fuzzy partition of the input space defined by a single neuron embeds the core of the information used by the neural network to perform its prediction.
